participantActionRequired.description: Obtain BCI criminal history record. Request a criminal history record from BCI. It is not a statutory attachment but it is the only practical way to assemble the full docket that ORC 2953.61 makes decisive.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Ohio Bureau of Criminal Identification and Investigation

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "What other Ohio cases do you have, in any court?" against BCI criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Certified disposition for each charge from the incident. Ask the clerk of each court for a certified copy of the disposition. Every charge from the incident is needed, not only the one the participant wants cleared.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The clerk of each court that handled a charge

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "What every charge was that came out of the same incident, and how each one ended." against Certified disposition for each charge from the incident, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Signature on the application — The court's application to seal or expunge.
Transcribing the drafted content onto the court's own application — The local court packet.
Attending the hearing — The sentencing or trial court, 45 to 90 days after filing.
Sending the signed order to BCI with the Sealings and Expungements Request — After the order, to BCI.
The participant signs the application.
Not identified; local practice may require it.
The review records that no fee is charged for non-conviction sealing, citing Ohio Legal Help rather than the statute. That is recorded below as an open question and the packet does not state a price.
Not applicable if no fee is charged; the general indigency exemption applies where one is.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: None by the participant. The court gives notice.
File with the clerk of the court where the case was pending, dismissed or tried, or where the no bill was reported, on that court's application.
